fields.title: Bound the Image Before Controlling the Quotient
fields.keywords: uniform-continuity, boundedness, image, quotient, denominator, api-chain
fields.how: own mechanism: When an estimate involves a quotient of uniformly continuous functions, get the boundedness of the image first as its own lemma; the quotient control depends on it and cannot be obtained alongside it. (source: this pattern's ! conclusion line; L8 rationale-backfill, zai-1, 2026-09-05)

context.text:
An analysis obligation where a uniformly continuous function's
    values appear in a denominator or in a ratio, and the target estimate mixes
    the continuity modulus with the size of the values.

IF.text:
The domain is bounded — or totally bounded — then uniform continuity gives
      a bounded image through a short chain of library steps, and that bound is
      the constant every subsequent quotient estimate needs.

HOWEVER.text:
Attempting the quotient bound directly entangles two independent facts: how
      fast the function varies, and how large it gets. The modulus of continuity
      says nothing about the latter, so an argument that needs both and has
      proved neither separately will stall at a point where it is unclear which
      is missing. The order matters more than the difficulty: the boundedness
      step is short, and having it in hand makes the quotient step routine.

THEN.text:
State and prove the boundedness of the image as its own lemma, via the
      uniform-continuity-to-bounded-image chain.

      Only then estimate the quotient, using that bound for the denominator and
      the modulus for the variation, keeping the two roles visibly distinct.

BECAUSE.text:
Uniform continuity is a hypothesis about differences and boundedness is a
      conclusion about values, and the step between them is exactly where the
      domain's boundedness enters. Proving them in one motion hides that entry
      point, so a proof that fails gives no signal about whether the domain
      hypothesis was too weak or the estimate was arranged badly. Separated, the
      failure names itself.

NEXT-STEPS.text:
next[Prove the image is bounded as a standalone lemma from uniform continuity.]
    next[Identify where the domain's boundedness enters and state it explicitly.]
    next[Estimate the quotient using the value bound for the denominator and the modulus for the variation.]

fields.title: Estimate by Bounding
fields.keywords: bound, estimate, inequality, upper, lower, dominate, majorise, triangle, Cauchy-Schwarz, Jensen

context.text:
You need to control a quantity (an integral, a sum, a probability, a norm) but
    exact computation is infeasible or unnecessary.

IF.text:
You need an upper bound (or lower bound) rather than an exact value, and standard
      inequalities (triangle, Cauchy-Schwarz, Jensen, Markov, Chebyshev, AM-GM) are
      available.

HOWEVER.text:
Bounds lose information. A bound that is too loose is useless. The art is in choosing
      the tightest bound that remains tractable. Chaining too many inequalities can
      accumulate slack to the point of triviality.

THEN.text:
Identify which direction you need (upper or lower). Apply the most appropriate
      standard inequality. Check that the resulting bound is tight enough for your
      purposes. If not, try a different inequality or a more refined decomposition
      before bounding.

BECAUSE.text:
Estimation is the engine of analysis and probability. Most theorems in these fields
      are proved by chains of inequalities, each replacing something complicated with
      something simpler. Knowing which inequality to reach for is a core skill.

NEXT-STEPS.text:
next[Determine whether you need an upper or lower bound.]
    next[Identify candidate inequalities from your toolbox.]
    next[Apply and check tightness — is the bound strong enough?]

fields.how: own mechanism: Prove something locally (on small pieces) and then assemble the local results into a global one. (source: this pattern's ! conclusion line; L8 rationale-backfill, zai-1, 2026-09-05)

context.text: You want to establish a property of a large or complicated object.

IF.text:
The object admits a decomposition into simpler pieces (open cover, partition, filtration,
      localisation at primes), and the property you want can be checked on pieces.

HOWEVER.text:
Not every property is local. You must verify that local data can be patched: the pieces
      must be compatible on overlaps, and the patching procedure must not introduce new problems.

THEN.text:
Cover the object with pieces where the property is manageable. Prove it on each piece.
      Check compatibility on overlaps. Glue the local results into a global one, using
      partitions of unity, sheaf conditions, or patching lemmas as appropriate.

BECAUSE.text:
Local-to-global is one of the deepest recurring themes in mathematics: sheaf theory,
      Mayer-Vietoris, local-global principles in number theory, partitions of unity in
      differential geometry. The power comes from reducing a hard global problem to many
      easy local ones.

NEXT-STEPS.text:
next[Decompose the object into local pieces.]
    next[Verify the property on each piece.]
    next[Check compatibility and assemble the global result.]

fields.how: own mechanism: When stuck, go back to the definition and write out exactly what it says. (source: this pattern's ! conclusion line; L8 rationale-backfill, zai-1, 2026-09-05)

context.text: You need to prove or use a property of an object, and the path forward is not clear.

IF.text:
The statement involves a defined concept (compact, continuous, exact, measurable, adjoint)
      and you are treating it as a black box instead of engaging with its content.

HOWEVER.text:
Definitions can unfold into multiple equivalent characterisations, and not all unfoldings
      are equally useful. Choosing the wrong characterisation can make the problem harder.

THEN.text:
Write out the definition of every technical term in the statement. Replace defined terms
      with their meanings. The proof obligation often becomes clear once the definitions are
      fully expanded. If multiple equivalent definitions exist, try each one.

BECAUSE.text:
Most proofs at the textbook level consist of nothing more than carefully unfolding
      definitions. "I don't see how to start" almost always means "I haven't written out
      what the words mean."

NEXT-STEPS.text:
next[Identify which terms in the statement are defined concepts.]
    next[Write out each definition fully.]
    next[See which unfolding makes the proof obligation match your tools.]
